I am old now, 76 years, and I farm the same 8 mu with my wife. My back is not what it was, so I do what I know works. I went to school only a few years, so I mostly do what my father did and what I see my neighbors doing.

I will keep 2 mu for cotton — we have grown cotton on that plot for many years, the soil suits it. The other 6 mu I do wheat and then maize, same as everyone here. Two crops from one land in one year — that is how we eat and sell a little.

For wheat, I sow in October. I use the improved seed from the dealer in town — everyone uses it now, the old seeds give too little. Before sowing I spread compound fertilizer, about 2 bags for my 6 mu, that is around 17 kg of nitrogen per mu with some phosphorus and potassium mixed in. In spring when wheat turns green I top-dress urea, about half a bag per mu. I water 3 times — before winter, at jointing, and at filling. My well works well. Pesticide I spray 2 times, for aphids and the head disease.

For maize after wheat, I plant quickly in June, hybrid seed, no time to waste. I put fertilizer at sowing and again at big trumpet stage. About 18 kg nitrogen per mu total — maize is hungry, if I give too little the cobs are small. Water 2 times if rain is not enough. Spray 1 time for the borer.

Cotton on 2 mu — I know cotton is troublesome, many sprays for bollworm, but the price is good some years. I use the Bt seed, less spraying than before but still I spray 4 times. Fertilizer about 15 kg N. Water 2 or 3 times.

I plough-turn the soil only for cotton before spring planting. For wheat and maize I just use rotary from the tractor man in the village — cheaper and my land is small.

I do not change much from last year. Changing is risky at my age.
